Who we are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work , and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Sr. Global Event Manager, Event Content Strategy and Event Production.

This position is needed to lead event content strategy, agenda architecture, speaker experience, and production readiness across Twilio’s priority flagship and internal events.

This role serves as an in-house event content strategist and executive producer for high-visibility programs including SIGNAL, SIGNAL World Tour, and SKO. You will translate business priorities, product narratives, audience needs, speaker moments, and production requirements into cohesive, high-quality event experiences that are strategically sound, operationally feasible, and polished onsite.

· Lead content strategy, session architecture, speaker experience, and production readiness across priority Global Events programs.

· Translate business objectives, product priorities, audience needs, and executive direction across sessions for keynotes, breakouts, workshops, executive sessions, livestream, on-demand content, and special programming.

· Develop agenda frameworks in partnership with the flagship events team across general sessions, breakouts, workshops, customer moments, sponsor content, executive programs, and special experiences to ensure strong attendee value and alignment to business, product, and GTM priorities.

· Partner with Product Marketing, Customer Marketing, Brand, Creative, Legal, Developer Network, Sales, executive stakeholders, production partners, and the broader Global Events team to drive alignment across content, agenda, speaker, and production workstreams.

· Define and maintain production standards across general session, breakout rooms, livestream, on-demand content, and priority content experiences to ensure production decisions support the event narrative, speaker needs, audience engagement, accessibility, and Twilio brand expectations.

· Oversee speaker readiness strategy, including milestone planning, rehearsal approach, deck review timelines, know-before-you-go communications, content lock dates, and onsite support models for executives, customers, internal speakers, partners, and breakout speakers.

· Guide content operations workflows, including call for presentations, CMS / Sessionboard management, agenda data, session metadata, speaker records, reporting, dashboards, deck tracking, brand / legal review, and production handoffs.

· Manage production partner and AVL collaboration by defining technical requirements, reviewing production scope, supporting vendor selection, and ensuring production plans are realistic, cost-conscious, and aligned to Twilio standards.

· Create and maintain integrated workbacks, decision paths, escalation models, playbooks, templates, review workflows, and operating models that enable cross-functional teams to execute with clarity.

· Identify content, speaker, agenda, and production risks early; escalate blockers clearly; recommend solutions; and drive timely decisions with the appropriate stakeholders.

· Lead post-event retrospectives for content, agenda, speaker experience, and production workstreams, capturing learnings and improving scalable playbooks for future programs.

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

· 7+ years of experience in event content strategy, event production, agenda development, speaker experience, executive events, or large-scale B2B event programming.

· Experience serving as an internal Executive Producer, senior content lead, or senior production lead for complex events with multiple stages, speaker types, stakeholder groups, and production dependencies.

· Experience building event content strategies that connect business priorities, audience needs, agenda architecture, speaker strategy, and production execution into a cohesive attendee experience.

· Experience working with executive stakeholders and cross-functional partners, including Product Marketing, Customer Marketing, Brand, Creative, Legal, Developer Relations, Sales, production partners, and event teams.

· Strong understanding of production planning, show flow, stage experience, breakout production, livestream, on-demand content, rehearsal planning, and onsite execution.

· Experience overseeing content operations workflows, including CFP, CMS or agenda management, speaker resources, deck collection, brand / legal review, and production lock.

· Strong project management skills, including the ability to build workbacks, playbooks, templates, escalation paths, decision logs, and operating models that help teams execute with clarity.

· Excellent communication, executive presence, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders, communicate tradeoffs, and make clear recommendations in complex or ambiguous situations.

· High attention to detail and a strong quality bar for narrative clarity, attendee experience, speaker readiness, brand alignment, and production polish.

· Experience supporting large-scale technology, SaaS, developer, customer, sales, or executive events.

· Experience with event content platforms, agenda management tools, CMS workflows, or speaker management systems such as Sessionboard, Swoogo, RainFocus, Airtable, or similar tools.

· Experience partnering with Product Marketing or Brand teams on keynote narratives, product launches, demos, customer stories, or executive moments.

· Experience building scalable content, production, and speaker readiness playbooks across flagship, regional, internal, or repeatable event programs.

· Comfort operating in a fast-paced, matrixed environment with shifting priorities, multiple stakeholders, and high-visibility deadlines.

Location

This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in CA, CT, NJ, NY, PA, WA.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, approximately 15% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way.

Join the team as Twilio’s next Senior Global Event Manager, Event Content Operations & Production.

Twilio’s most important events require strong operational leadership, thoughtful production strategy, disciplined systems, and clear accountability across teams, vendors, and deadlines.

As Global Event Manager, Content Operations & Production, you will lead the operational and production strategy that turns Twilio’s event content plans into polished, scalable live experiences. You will own content operations, production-partner management, event content systems, technical readiness, and onsite delivery across the Global Events portfolio.

You will serve as the content and production lead for SIGNAL World Tour, owning the production model, agency partnership, content workflows, and onsite execution for priority Tier 1 events. For SIGNAL, you will lead breakout content operations and production and partner on General Session production support, including technical planning, production readiness, and vendor coordination. For SKO, you will own production-partner strategy and delivery.

This role is a strong fit for someone who combines production expertise with operational rigor and knows how to build delivery models that scale globally.

· Set the content operations and production strategy across Twilio’s priority Global Events portfolio, with primary focus on SIGNAL and SKO.

· Lead SIGNAL breakout content operations and production, including CFP, session intake and selection workflows, agenda and speaker data, deck readiness, technical checks, Speaker Ready Room, and onsite delivery.

· Partner on SIGNAL General Session production, providing senior leadership across technical planning, rehearsals, vendor coordination, and show readiness.

· Own SKO production strategy and delivery, including production-partner scope, technical planning, budget oversight, rehearsals, and onsite execution.

· Lead production agencies and vendors across priority programs, setting scope, standards, budgets, deliverables, performance expectations, and escalation paths.

· Own the event content systems and technology strategy, including Sessionboard and related platforms, and ensure accurate, connected data across agenda, speaker, content, and production workflows.

· Establish scalable operating models for content intake, agenda management, deck delivery, production handoffs, reporting, and onsite execution.

· Operationalize the speaker communications and experience standards established by the Sr. Global Event Manager, Content Strategy & Speaker Experience through systems, processes, vendors, and onsite workflows.

· Serve as the content and production lead for SIGNAL World Tour in partnership with the Flagship Events Lead, providing strategic oversight of production planning, content operations, agency delivery, and Tier 1 onsite execution.

· Make senior-level decisions and recommendations across production approach, scope, budget, resourcing, technology, operational feasibility, risk, and attendee experience.

· Serve as the senior escalation point for content operations, production, systems, and vendor risks, driving timely resolution across cross-functional teams.

· Build reusable production, technology, data-governance, and content-operations standards that scale across flagship, internal, regional, and executive programs.

· Lead post-event evaluations across production, systems, agency performance, and operational delivery, turning insights into improvements across the portfolio.

· Direct agencies, vendors, contractors, and supporting resources while retaining accountability for quality, budget, and final delivery.

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

· 7+ years in event production, content operations, event technology, or large-scale B2B events.

· Proven leadership of complex event production across multiple programs, stages, vendors, stakeholders, and deadlines.

· Demonstrated ownership of production strategy, technical planning, budgets, scopes of work, vendor management, risk, and onsite delivery.

· Deep knowledge of breakout content operations, including CFP, session intake, agenda management, deck readiness, technical checks, and Speaker Ready Room.

· Hands-on proficiency with event content systems and agenda platforms, including session data, speaker records, reporting, and production handoffs.

· Strong command of General Session and breakout production, rehearsals, show flow, livestream or recorded content, and onsite execution.

· Sound judgment when making tradeoffs across scope, budget, timeline, technology, production quality, and attendee experience.

· Strong cross-functional leadership, stakeholder management, and operational decision-making skills.

· A track record of building scalable operating models, governance, standards, and playbooks.

· Ability to lead agencies, vendors, contractors, and supporting resources while retaining accountability for final delivery.

· Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally.

· Background leading production or content operations for a global roadshow or regional event portfolio.

· Familiarity with large-scale technology, SaaS, developer, customer, sales, or executive events.

· Hands-on knowledge of Sessionboard, Swoogo, RainFocus, Airtable, Cvent, or similar platforms.

· Fluency in production budgeting, vendor negotiations, and change-order management.

· Strong partnership skills across Product Marketing, Customer Marketing, Brand, Creative, Legal, Sales Enablement, regional marketing, and executive stakeholders.

· Knowledge of livestream, broadcast, recording, and on-demand content workflows.

· Comfort operating in a fast-paced, highly matrixed global environment.

Location

This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in CA, CT, NJ, NY, PA, WA.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, approximately 20% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way.

Hey there!

We’re Fever , the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

What is Candlelight?

· Candlelight concerts are a unique musical and sensory experience created by the stunning ambience of candlelight. These concerts allow you to enjoy some of the most famous works of classical music in a completely new way and in various spectacular locations.

· The concerts highlight talent from upcoming talent to professional musicians

· Candlelight is now expanding beyond classical music into other genres that fit well within the experience such as jazz, soul, flamenco, opera, and more.

We are seeking Event Managers to join our on site events team in Debrecen to assist and manage Fever Originals’ flagship experience, Candlelight. This position is freelance and with flexible hours varying month to month dependent on availability, which may be extended, lead to other Fever Originals event work or permanent opportunities in the future.

Du brennst für Events und liebst es, Menschen zusammenzubringen? Ob Kundenanlass, Fachkonferenz oder internes Teamevent – du sorgst dafür, dass jedes Event unvergesslich wird. Gleichzeitig fühlst du dich in der Marketingwelt zuhause und es motiviert dich, dich in einem dynamischen Umfeld rund um Business Software Lösungen zu bewegen.
**Das macht deinen Alltag spannend:**
* Du machst unsere Events zu echten Erlebnissen. Denn von der ersten Idee bis zum letzten Applaus hältst du die Fäden in der Hand und begeisterst Kunden, Partner und Kolleg\*innen gleichermassen.
* Mit frischen Event\-Konzepten setzt du unsere Softwarelösungen gekonnt in Szene und sorgst dafür, dass sie nicht nur verstanden, sondern erlebt werden.
* Du jonglierst souverän mit allen Beteiligten. Sei dies intern wie extern, von Location bis Technik, von Speaker bis Dienstleister.
* Ob Einladung, Landingpage, Mailings oder Aftermovie: Du bringst unsere Event\-Kommunikation auf den Punkt und gibst jedem Anlass die nötige Strahlkraft.
* Kleinere Events moderierst du selbstbewusst oder sorgst dafür, dass unsere Expert\*innen im perfekten Setup glänzen können.
* Mit deinem Blick fürs Ganze hältst du das Budget im Griff, misst den Erfolg und optimierst, wo es sinnvoll ist.
* Passende Werbeartikel und Give\-aways finden dank dir den Weg zu Kunden und Mitarbeitenden.
* Und weil Events nicht alles sind: Du entwickelst auch Marketing\- und Kampagnenideen, die unsere Anlässe pushen und unsere Leistungen sichtbar machen.
* Ins Marketingteam bringst du frischen Wind, kreative Inputs und jede Menge Teamspirit mit, damit wir gemeinsam unsere Events auf das nächste Level heben.
**Das bringst du mit:**
* Du hast eine Ausbildung im Marketing\-, Event\- oder Kommunikationsbereich oder bist auf einem anderen Weg dorthin gekommen und weisst genau, was du kannst.
* Erste Erfahrungen in der Eventorganisation und im Marketing hast du bereits gesammelt und fühlst dich in einem dynamischen IT\-Umfeld wohl.
* Events sind dein Ding! Du sprudelst vor Ideen, liebst kreative Lösungen und probierst gerne Neues aus.
* Du gehst deinen Alltag strukturiert und selbständig an und übernimmst gerne Verantwortung. Ruhe bewahrst du auch dann, wenn mehrere Projekte gleichzeitig laufen.
* Stilsicheres Deutsch ist für dich selbstverständlich, denn eine klare Kommunikation ist Gold wert.
* Deine Kolleginnen und Kollegen freuen sich auf Verstärkung von einer unkomplizierten Persönlichkeit, die gerne lacht, auch über sich selber.
**Und das hast du dann davon:**
* Ein Job, der garantiert nicht langweilig wird: Mit klarem Fokus auf Events gestaltest du richtig viel und bekommst den Freiraum, deine Ideen gross zu machen.
* Ein Team, das dich unterstützt und einen Teamspirit, der bei Kununu schon fünf Sterne bekommen hat.
* Von null auf hundert in 19… nein, nicht Sekunden, Jahren. Wir sind schnell, aber gesund gewachsen und gut organisiert. Doch etwas ist noch wie in unseren Anfängen: Die Strukturen sind schlank und du findest die richtigen Ansprechpartner leicht.
* Sobald du im Job angekommen bist, warten spannende Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten auf dich.
* Einen guten Lohn, den du mit deiner Leistung mitbestimmen kannst. Krankentaggeld\- und Unfallversicherung? Übernehmen wir. Zusammen mit anderen Benefits macht das schnell noch einmal ein paar Tausender im Jahr aus.
Wir hätten noch viel mehr zu erzählen. Was deinen Job bei uns sonst noch spannend macht zum Beispiel. Wer wir sind und wie wir so ticken. Deshalb zögere nicht und macht dir dein eigenes Bild.
**Schon Feuer gefangen?**Du willst lieber schon heute als morgen loslegen? Dann her mit deinem CV oder dem Link auf dein LinkedIn\-Profil. Das Motivationsschreiben kannst du dir sparen, wir sind auch da völlig unkompliziert.
**Und das (a) im Stellentitel?**Es ist unser Statement für Vielfalt. Wir stehen auf durchmischte Teams. Alter, Herkunft, Hautfarbe oder Geschlecht sind uns egal. Bei uns sind **(a)**lle willkommen, die uns mit ihrem Talent weiterbringen.

Hey there!
We’re Fever , the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.
Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.
Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.
Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?
To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!
Ready to be part of the experience?
Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.
Freelance Event Manager
Location : Cambridge
Contract : Ongoing
Working Pattern : Flexible, with evenings, weekends and public holidays required depending on the event.
Reports to : Producer / Project Lead
Manages : Event staff, including front-of-house, bar and support staff where required

We, at Fever, are looking for enthusiastic, experienced Freelance Event Managers to help deliver a series of smaller-scale live events.
This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys being involved in every stage of an event — from helping build and prepare the space, to managing staff and suppliers, welcoming guests, keeping things running smoothly during the event, and making sure everything is packed down properly at the end.
We’re looking for someone who is organised, proactive and confident taking ownership on the ground. You’ll need to be comfortable getting stuck in and doing whatever is needed to help create a successful event.
A background in events, hospitality, bars, venues or visitor experiences would be particularly useful.

Event Delivery
· Take ownership of the on-the-ground delivery of events, from set-up through to breakdown.
· Work closely with the wider production team to prepare the event space and ensure everything is ready for guests.
· Coordinate event staff, suppliers, venues and contractors as required.
· Oversee the smooth running of the event, responding quickly and calmly to any issues that arise.
· Be hands-on with set-up, furniture, signage, equipment, stock and general event preparation.
· Manage event breakdown and ensure the venue is left clean, tidy and to the agreed standard.
Team Management
· Brief and manage front-of-house, bar and other event staff.
· Coordinate staff rotas, breaks and responsibilities during events.
· Make sure everyone understands their role and is delivering a high standard of service.
· Lead by example and be willing to get involved wherever the team needs support.
· Manage any agency or temporary staff on-site where required.
Hospitality & Guest Experience
· Help create a welcoming, friendly and well-organised experience for guests.
· Oversee front-of-house and, where relevant, bar or hospitality operations.
· Monitor guest flow and respond to any customer queries or issues.
· Deal confidently and professionally with complaints or unexpected situations.
· Maintain high standards of cleanliness, presentation and customer service throughout the event.
Practical & Operational Support
· Work with venues and suppliers to ensure all logistical requirements are in place.
· Assist with deliveries, stock checks and equipment movement.
· Keep track of event supplies and flag any requirements or issues to the wider team.
· Troubleshoot practical problems on-site and find solutions quickly.
· Complete opening, closing and event checklists where required.
Health & Safety
· Ensure the event is operated safely and in accordance with venue and production requirements.
· Carry out basic safety checks of the event space.
· Make sure staff understand relevant health & safety and emergency procedures.
· Escalate and document any incidents or issues appropriately.
Communication & Reporting
· Provide clear updates to the Event Producer / Project Lead before, during and after events.
· Flag any operational issues, staffing concerns or supplier problems as early as possible.
· Complete basic post-event reporting and feedback where required.
· Help identify improvements that could make future events run more smoothly.

Previous experience managing or coordinating live events, hospitality operations, bars, venues or visitor experiences.
A practical, hands-on approach and a willingness to get stuck into whatever needs doing.
Confident managing people and taking responsibility for an event on the ground.
Highly organised, reliable and able to work independently.
Calm under pressure and comfortable making decisions when things don't go to plan.
Friendly, approachable and confident dealing with guests, staff, suppliers and venue teams.
Strong communication and problem-solving skills.
A genuine interest in creating great events and experiences.
Comfortable working flexible hours, including evenings, weekends and public holidays.

Most importantly, we’re looking for someone who doesn't mind getting their hands dirty.
Our events are smaller in scale, but we want them to feel polished, well-run and memorable. That means we need people who are happy to move between the big picture and the small details — whether that's briefing a team, helping set up a bar, moving furniture, sorting out a supplier issue or jumping in to help guests.
You don't need to have managed huge-scale events. Good practical experience, a positive attitude and the ability to take ownership are just as important.
This is a great opportunity for an experienced events or hospitality professional who enjoys freelance work and wants to be part of building exciting events from the ground up.

What is Candlelight?
Since July 2019, Fever Originals has produced a series of classical music concerts in a “candlelit setting” which take place in the most intimate and undiscovered venues all over the world.

Cities include: France (Paris, Toulouse, Lyon), Spain (Madrid, Barcelona, Seville, Valencia), Portugal (Lisbon and Porto), and the United States (Los Angeles, New York, and Chicago), and are in the process of expanding to your city!

Candlelight has democratized classical music by sharing it with the general public and providing a unique experience for each of our audiences. As of today, Candlelight concerts are present in over 300 cities around the world!
For this role, we are looking for a part-time onsite Event Manager for our Candlelight Concerts located in Honolulu, Hawaii . This is a part-time position that includes flexible weekday hours for preparation and planning, in addition to event support during our concerts. Most concerts take place on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings, so availability during those times may be expected.

· Act as main point of contact onsite for Candlelight events and staff; communicate directly with Fever Originals manager

· Drive uHaul with event supplies to and from concert venues (if a candidate is not able to drive or does not have a valid driver’s license, alternative methods of transporting supplies may be arranged)

· Manage inventory and track supplies for venues

· Manage any printing needs

· Manage guest lists for all events

· Manage the opening and closing remarks at events (this will usually consist of a recorded speech, but may require public speaking on an occasional basis)

· Weekly reporting to Fever Originals Project Managers about the status of each event; including both the pre and post-event findings and feedback

· Occasionally assist with evaluating and executing walk-throughs of potential venues

· Opportunity to partake in an exciting and rapidly growing company and the possibility to manage Candlelight and other Fever Original Events in other areas

· Represent both the Fever and Candlelight brand fully through professional communication and management; acting as the main customer service representative at every event

· 1+ years of experience in event management and/or a relevant degree (preferred)

· Interest and passion for live music and organizing events

· Exceptional customer service skills

· Experience leading an on-site team

· Strong problem-solving skills

· Good ability to work in a pressured environment

· Knowledge of AV and PA systems (desirable)

· The use of personal laptop will be required

· In effect Driver’s License is strongly preferred

The contract will be for 6 months, ideally starting as soon as possible. The shows run weekly and shift times vary from 4-8 hours/day. The role will be 29 hours max a week and possibly work on certain Holidays, (not including Thanksgiving or Christmas as there will be no concerts those days). There may be an opportunity to extend the contract at the end of the initial 6 months.
Rate : 25$/hour - further details can be discussed during the interview

Having many products and countries, we need to make sure everything runs smoothly. As the operations team, we help supervise operations across Fever teams and identify and prioritize needs. Our goal is to help Fever grow by improving the efficiency of our ways of working and maintaining a best-in-class experience for all stakeholders.
We are seeking an experienced and strategic Global Production Logistics Manager to lead Fever's global transportation operations end-to-end. In this role, you will lead a distributed team of logistics coordinators, set the strategy for global product movements and customs compliance, analyze strategic sourcing vs. local fabrication options, and act as the connective tissue between internal event production teams and external transport partners.

End-to-end transport & logistics management: Own global logistics and freight operations from start to finish, ensuring event assets move on time and cost-effectively, while acting quickly to resolve shipping disruptions and operational escalations.
Global trade & customs compliance: Oversee global import/export processes, temporary admissions (ATA Carnets), tariff classifications, and customs compliance to guarantee seamless international cross-border movements for live event productions.
Strategic sourcing vs. fabrication analysis: Evaluate total cost of ownership by comparing international shipping costs against local fabrication or sourcing options, advising production teams on optimal logistics strategies.
Cross-functional production integration: Partner closely with event production, finance, legal, and tax teams to align freight timelines with event setup schedules and foster seamless operational synergy.
Team leadership & mentorship: Lead and develop a distributed team of logistics coordinators, balancing workload, unblocking complex challenges, and scaling operational processes across global regions.
Vendor negotiation & 3PL management: Manage relationships with freight forwarders, customs brokers, and 3PL partners, negotiating competitive rates and service contracts on behalf of the logistics department.
KPIs, budget & SLA oversight: Establish, track, and report performance metrics (on-time delivery, freight spend variances, customs clearance lead times) to drive continuous cost optimization and operational excellence.
Continuous process improvement: Identify process inefficiencies, design standardized logistics frameworks, and build training programs to elevate internal transportation expertise.

Experience: 5+ years leading global logistics, freight forwarding, or production transportation operations, preferably within live events, entertainment, or high-volume global shipping.
Customs & trade expertise: Deep knowledge of international customs regulations, import/export compliance, HS codes, temporary importations (e.g., ATA Carnets), and duty optimization.
Team leadership: 3+ years of experience direct managing logistics coordinators or operations teams across multiple regions and time zones.
Strategic & financial analysis: Strong capability to analyze logistics trade-offs (e.g., shipping vs. local fabrication) and manage departmental budgets, vendor quotes, and KPIs.
Vendor negotiation: Proven track record negotiating high-value contracts and freight rates with global 3PLs, carriers, and customs brokers.
Education & tools: Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, or equivalent experience; proficiency in TMS/ERP platforms, Google Sheets/Excel, and analytics tools.
Communication & adaptability: Fluent English with excellent stakeholder management skills to explain complex trade/logistics issues to non-technical teams in a fast-paced environment.
